tasks.short: Prepare checked shipment completion reports and submit their final versions.

steps.what: Collect shipment completion evidence and resolve missing freight details
Capture the shipment report fields and exception account
Assemble completion reports from captured fields and the inspector's account
Check completion reports against shipment evidence and correct discrepancies
Submit the final shipment report to its designated recipient

tasks.design: Configure a completion evidence view and report form in {OPS_SYSTEM}; a native template fills the report in {DOCS}. The inspector captures exceptions, checks the report and separately submits its exact final version through {EMAIL}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Completion facts are repeatedly found and copied into reports.
tasks.enabler_now: Native report templates can reuse explicitly captured shipment fields.
tasks.still_hard: Incomplete records and disputed freight conditions require investigation.
tasks.human_edge: Resolve discrepancies and stand behind the reported account.

ambition.what: Review exceptions earlier while producing consistent completion reports.

tasks.altitude: Move from repeated assembly to evidence quality.

evidence.claim: Native views, forms and field-based templates could reduce shipment report assembly; the saving is an unmeasured E1 scenario.

assumptions: The scenario includes a real report submitted to an external shipment customer; internal-only reporting would use internal write authority.

The inspector produces shipment ID, completion date, origin, destination, freight condition, evidence references and exception text in s2, retaining 16 hours. Missing fields stop assembly and are resolved manually in s1 or s2.
Assembly s3 copies captured facts and the inspector's account without interpreting an inspection. Native settings and templates are tried before integration.
Source inspection work is not repeated here; locating and validating its existing evidence is counted in s1. Same-system saves have no separate saving.
unknowns: Existing completion fields and required report formats.
research_questions: Does native report assembly reduce total work after exception capture and checking?

already_counted.description: Capture report inputs and the inspector's exception account.

incremental.description: Maintain report fields, templates and mapping checks.

approvals.approved_version: Exact corrected final report, attachments and recipient; any alteration requires a fresh send-time check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1 scenario: B=100, R=61, gross=39; upkeep=5 yields central net=34. No saving is attributed to the final send or same-system save.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Inspect freight securing and record the bracing and blocking findings.

steps.what: Retrieve shipment specifications and applicable bracing and blocking instructions
Inspect shipments and assess whether freight is securely braced and blocked
Record the freight securing findings and any required corrections
Explain securing deficiencies and required corrections to the loading crew

tasks.design: Configure linked securing instructions in {DOCS} and a shipment-specific inspection form in {OPS_SYSTEM}. Retain the physical inspection, safety assessment and crew discussion; simplify only lookup and recording.
tasks.previous_blocker: Reference retrieval and repeated entry accompany physical securing checks.
tasks.enabler_now: Native reference links and reusable field layouts can reduce those supporting actions.
tasks.still_hard: Hidden defects and unusual loading arrangements need on-site judgement.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise unsafe securing and explain a correction suited to the actual load.
tasks.altitude: Make inspection records clearer while retaining the full safety assessment.

reach.learn: Link a finding to the observed restraint or blocking defect.

evidence.claim: Linked instructions and native inspection fields could shorten supporting lookup and entry, without automating physical securing assessment.

assumptions: This task owns the securing inspection checklist; the separate freight conditions task records handling events and other condition details rather than copying this checklist.

The inspector enters shipment ID, restraint or blocking location, observed defect and required correction in s3; 10.5 retained hours include capture and correction. No automated safety verdict consumes these fields.
Crew communication here is within the organisation and uses internal authority. There is no added formal approval or autonomous release of freight.
Try native forms and linked document views first; ordinary internal saves do not create an additional saving.
unknowns: Inspection checklist and current reference retrieval time.
research_questions: Can a native form reduce recording time without hiding unusual securing defects?

already_counted.description: Capture and correct securing findings in the native inspection form.

incremental.description: Keep inspection fields and instruction links current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1 scenario: B=100, R=93.5, gross=6.5; upkeep=1.5 gives central net=5. Physical inspection and crew communication retain all their time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Record freight condition, handling events and encountered problems with traceable observations.

steps.what: Locate the freight identity and existing condition or handling records
Observe freight conditions and clarify handling events and problems with witnesses
Record condition fields, handling times and the provenance of reported problems
Write the freight problem narrative and distinguish observations from disputed accounts
Check freight details and correct omissions or unsupported statements

tasks.design: Use a native freight form in {OPS_SYSTEM} with linked prior entries and a condition narrative template in {DOCS}. Separate observation and witness conversations from the actual record write; the inspector retains attribution and correction.
tasks.previous_blocker: Freight details and event accounts must be assembled and written repeatedly.
tasks.enabler_now: Native field layouts and narrative headings can reduce navigation and repeated wording.
tasks.still_hard: Conflicting accounts cannot be turned into certain facts by a form.
tasks.human_edge: Record what was observed, who reported an event and what remains uncertain.

ambition.what: Spot recurring handling issues from more consistent condition records.

tasks.altitude: Improve record quality rather than automate factual judgement.

reach.task: Interpret recorded damage and handling events
reach.learn: Distinguish observed conditions from attributed statements.

evidence.claim: Native freight forms and narrative templates could reduce recording effort; observation and attribution remain human work.

assumptions: This task owns condition and handling event records; securing inspection findings are referenced, not rewritten or credited again.

The inspector produces freight ID, event time, location, condition, witness attribution and unresolved issue fields in s3, retaining 21 hours. Missing times or disputed accounts remain explicitly unknown and are manually clarified.
A template supplies headings and reusable factual labels, not a generated condition verdict. There is no model loop or hidden machine write.
Native views and templates precede any custom app; same-system save time is negligible and earns no separate saving.
unknowns: Current record layout and frequency of disputed event accounts.
research_questions: Do structured fields reduce total entry and correction time while preserving provenance?

already_counted.description: Enter and correct the condition fields and event provenance.

incremental.description: Maintain record layout, narrative headings and field guidance.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1 scenario: B=100, R=85, gross=15; upkeep=3 yields central net=12. Observation, witness clarification and final correction retain all their time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Prepare and explain cargo-specific stowage advice to crews.

steps.what: Retrieve dangerous cargo instructions and heavy load stowage references
Examine the cargo arrangement and clarify the crews' stowage questions
Determine suitable stowing techniques for the dangerous or heavy cargo
Write the cargo-specific stowage briefing notes
Advise crews on the selected techniques and check their understanding
Record the stowage guidance given and unresolved crew questions

tasks.design: Configure linked stowage references and a briefing template in {DOCS}, with a compact advice record in {OPS_SYSTEM}. Keep cargo assessment, technique selection and crew explanation with the inspector; no software certifies safe stowage.
tasks.previous_blocker: Relevant instructions and briefing wording are repeatedly assembled.
tasks.enabler_now: Native reference collections and briefing headings can support preparation.
tasks.still_hard: The actual load, vessel or vehicle constraints and crew understanding determine applicability.
tasks.human_edge: Adapt safe advice to the cargo and recognise when specialist support is needed.
tasks.altitude: Prepare clearer cargo-specific guidance without delegating safety judgement.

reach.learn: Recognise the limits of the advice for a changed load.

evidence.claim: The digest describes a warning that some inland stowage programs do not match stability manuals; this cautions against treating software output as a safety verdict.
Native reference links, briefing headings and advice fields could shorten preparation and recording; this is an unmeasured E1 scenario.

assumptions: This scenario includes existing briefing notes and an advice record; those writes are separately priced rather than folded into the crew conversation. If no written briefing exists, its preparation saving does not apply.

The inspector chooses references in s1, produces cargo constraints in s2 and writes selected techniques and limitations in s4, retaining 11.25 hours. Missing cargo facts cause manual clarification rather than guessed advice.
Crews here are colleagues, so the discussion uses internal authority. No new approval procedure or external send is introduced.
Native templates and reference views come first. A same-system save is incidental and contributes no separate saving.
unknowns: Existing briefing documentation and specialist escalation requirements.
research_questions: Can linked instructions and briefing headings reduce preparation while preserving cargo-specific limitations?

already_counted.description: Write cargo-specific briefing notes using the template.

incremental.description: Maintain the reference set and briefing headings.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1 documented-briefing scenario: B=100, R=92.25, gross=7.75; upkeep=2 gives central net=5.75. Assessment, selection and crew explanation retain all their time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Retain physical freight and safety judgement while improving traceable records and reports.
reach: Connect observed freight conditions with complete reports and practical crew guidance.
role.ambitious_version: A transportation inspector who produces clear, timely records while personally assessing safety and explaining cargo-specific corrections.
